Survived something everyone believes killed them, under a different name
The original identity, if revealed, carries baggage that would end the current one
Has been maintaining a cover-up of a past institutional failure that cost lives
Exposure means accountability for something that happened a long time ago, to real people
Was the informant whose report triggered a purge that destroyed innocent lives
The report was accurate in some ways but deliberately misleading in others
Possesses an original copy of a document that was officially declared destroyed
The document changes the legitimacy of something very important to very powerful people
The person who raised them was not their parent, and that parent is someone significant
The revelation would disrupt inheritance, property, and several people's sense of identity
Was captured and released under terms they have never disclosed
The terms may mean they owe something to an enemy that they haven't paid yet
Knows that the decisive victory everyone celebrates was won through treachery, not skill
Several people built careers on that victory; they would not appreciate the truth
Has been quietly betting against the ventures they talk their neighbours into, and profiting when they fail
Civil fraud liability and the permanent destruction of a reputation built over decades
The goods they sell as locally produced are sourced from somewhere with exploitative labour practices
The premium they charge depends entirely on the lie holding
Has been paying a health official to suppress a finding about their product
People are being harmed; the official is growing nervous; the finding is documented
Has information about a competitor that would ruin them, obtained through clearly illegal means
Using the information exposes how it was obtained; not using it means watching an advantage expire
Their business partner died of natural causes that weren't entirely natural
An investigation would find ambiguous evidence: enough to ruin, maybe enough to prosecute
Is a member of a group that faces serious persecution, and passes for something else entirely
Discovery ends everything they have built; some of the people closest to them would turn on them
Their celebrated origin story is a fabrication they created to escape an intolerable past
The real past includes people who are still alive and who remember
Has been corresponding with someone they are publicly required to treat as an enemy
The correspondence is genuine and affectionate; it would be read as treason
Lives a second life under a different name in another part of the settlement or a nearby town
The two lives have begun to approach each other geographically
Is not who their documents say they are. The real person died years ago and they took the identity
The real person's family recently moved to the area
Lost their faith completely but maintains the role. It's just a job now
Discovery destroys their flock's trust and their own standing; some would call it heresy
Has been covering for a colleague's heretical activities out of personal loyalty
When the colleague is exposed (and they will be), this secret comes with them
Has been systematically falsifying miracle reports for decades
A sceptical investigator with the right access could unravel it all in a week
Knows their religious order was founded on a historical lie
The truth would shatter the institution they've dedicated their life to
Possesses a relic that was officially declared destroyed, and kept it because they couldn't face destroying something real
Possession is heresy; surrender means explaining how they had it
Gave an order during a battle that caused friendly casualties. It was covered up as enemy action
The families of the dead believe a lie that this person actively maintains
Has been selling patrol routes and schedules to someone outside the settlement
People have already died as a result; they are rationalising this as survivable
Has been skimming from military supply budgets for years through a trusted subordinate
The subordinate now knows enough to destroy them, and is becoming expensive
Was ordered to commit an atrocity and complied, and has since risen in the organisation that ordered it
The order came from someone senior; exposure implicates both of them
A sealed letter arrived for them three weeks ago. They haven't opened it. They won't say why.
They've been quietly buying up property in a district that hasn't been announced as a development site. Yet.
One of their staff has started asking questions about records from seven years ago. They've been reassigned twice already.
A merchant they spoke against has started praising them in public, and will not say why.
Their most trusted advisor hasn't been seen in four days. The official story changes each time it's told.
They know who committed a crime the guard is currently investigating. They're not telling the guard.
Someone has been leaving anonymous notes in their office pointing to a colleague's corruption. The notes are accurate.
They've been meeting privately with someone from outside the settlement whose identity they won't disclose.
A routine appointment they made three weeks ago has been rescheduled four times. Each time they initiated the change.
Someone who publicly supports them is being paid by someone who opposes them. They know this.
They received a deposition in a civil case that, if acted on, would be correct, and would ruin someone they need.
A clerk in their office has been copying letters at night, and the copies have turned up in a rival's hands.
They signed an order last month on bad information, and the family it ruined has learned whose seal is on it.
A petition they set aside has gathered names from half their street, and the people who signed it want an answer this week.

Polite enough; keeps people back from the drying racks and the kiln.

Generous with a cup and with talk; hears everything the taverns say.
Practical, with the red hands of someone who works hot vats all day.

Watchful around the vats and the store. Keeps the back of the brewery locked.
Pleasant at the front; does not show anyone the back.

Strong, careful hands and an eye that checks every stave for a crack.

Easy and chatty, with the steady rhythm of hammer and hoop behind every sentence.

Short and busy. The yard is full of half-made casks and every one is late.

Upright and watchful, with a habit of standing where they can see the whole room.
Polite and brief; asks your business, your lodgings and how long you plan to stay.
Tired but sharp, with the patience of someone used to hearing complaints all day.

Busy and short with outsiders. The watch has its own business to see to.
Answers briefly and suggests you keep out of trouble.
the master of granaries

Neat and careful, with dust in the folds of the coat and a tally board under one arm.

Always on the way somewhere, keys in hand. Treats every question as a delay.
Says what is needed and nothing more; points you to a clerk.

Short and hot-tempered, with no patience for anyone who gets in the way of the work.

Watchful of the furnace and the people near it. Moves visitors back without asking.
Talks about the trade, but not about the workers or the stream.

Warm in every sense: flour on the arms, the smell of bread, a cheerful greeting before dawn.

Up since the middle of the night and quick about everything. The queue moves fast.
Sells what is baked; special orders by the day before, paid on collection.
Watches the till and the trays with equal care.
Polite and brief; does not give credit to anyone they do not know.

Eager to hear about any road you have travelled, and quick to write down what you say.

Sells copies at a fair rate; a fresh survey costs a great deal and takes a season.

Sawdust everywhere, a loud voice and hands missing the tip of one finger.
Cuts to measure and sells by the length; wants the order written and half paid.
Busy and impatient. The saws run all day and every stop costs money.

Easy and open, smelling of fresh pine. Likes to talk about wood more than most people do.
Tells you which timber is good this year and who has been buying it.

Calm, unhurried and kind, with the steady hands of someone who has seen every kind of night.

Watchful and private. People lower their voices as the midwife passes.
Will help anyone in need; says nothing about anyone else's household.
Brisk, practical and tired. Asks how far along, how far away and when.
Comes when called and takes what the family can give; remembers who never pays.
the senior charter master

Generous with advice about the work and the dangers; slower to hand out the best jobs.

Proud of the craft, with a habit of handing visitors small pieces to admire.
Explains how a thing is made and what it is worth; enjoys an appreciative audience.

Polite; does not talk about how the colours are made.

Loud, theatrical and flattering, with a hand on your arm before you have finished your name.

Lets you meet the calmer animals and explains how each was trained.

Watches every traveller coming and remembers them going.

Bored and glad of company, with gossip about everyone who has crossed this week.
Talks about the road and the travellers; knows who has passed and when.
Sells cheap wine poured into the casks of a famous vintage

Black with soot to the elbows, eyes red from the smoke. Says little to people from outside the woods.

Practical and plain. Talks in sacks and loads.

Glad of company in the woods, with a pot always on the fire.

Has been storing a smuggler's goods among the furs in the back room

Smooth and flattering. Drapes a fur over your shoulders before you can say no.
